title: Idempotent Tool-Calling Executor
summary: Build a tool executor that safely handles a model retrying the same tool call, validates arguments against a schema, and surfaces errors the model can act on.
requirements: Validate a tool call's name against a registry before execution.
Validate required arguments are present before execution.
Execute idempotently: a repeated call ID returns the cached result without re-running the handler.
A failed handler attempt must NOT be cached, so a retry with the same call ID gets a real second attempt.
start: Start from Module 4's exercise function and wire it to 2-3 real mock tools (e.g. a fake 'send_email' and 'create_ticket') with their own schemas, instead of the single test-mock tool used in the exercise.
acceptance: An unknown tool name is rejected with a structured error before any handler runs.
A missing required argument is rejected before any handler runs.
Calling the same tool with the same call ID twice only invokes the handler once, both calls return the identical cached result.
A handler that raises returns a structured failure and is NOT cached, a retry with the same call ID gets a genuine second attempt.
Two different call IDs for the same tool execute independently (not falsely deduplicated).
tests: Unknown tool name → rejected, handler call count stays 0.
Missing required argument → rejected, handler call count stays 0.
Same call ID called twice → handler call count is 1, both results identical.
Handler raises on first call, succeeds on second call with the SAME call ID → first result is a structured failure, second is a success.
Two different call IDs, same tool → handler call count is 2.
mistakes: Checking the idempotency cache after invoking the handler instead of before.
Caching a result before confirming the handler actually succeeded.
Deduplicating based on argument similarity instead of call ID, incorrectly blocking legitimate independent calls.
solution: Look up the tool in the registry, reject if missing.
Validate every required field is present in the arguments.
Check the idempotency store for the call ID, return the cached value if present.
Try/except the handler call: on success cache and return; on failure return a structured error WITHOUT caching.
